chapter: Childhood, Mardi Gras and first brass band
title: Mardi Gras in his youth and masking with a clarinet
summary: He recalls masked groups, and once masked and played clarinet in the street.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: When was the first parade you ever saw that you can remember? Or anything like the Mardi Gras in those days, what they were like?
Oh, the Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras was something them days. That's better than now, I think.
You had so many people with masks in those days. You had, in those days you had monkeys and so many bunch of guys which you had to get all messy. Red Devil and skeletons and all that.
Is there any special music around then, more than there is now on Mardi Gras? Well, no. Is there groups playing in the street, aside from the brass bands, anything special?

Well you'd have a lot of people would get a high band on the truck. Yeah, well I did. You had a lot of that. But the people would just mask those days in groups and just go around the street and have their fun and talking to people, calling people in the name that they know, they know that they didn't know who they was. Have them guessing. Have you ever played in any of those early Mardi Gras, Albert?

No, but I'll tell you, when I first started to learn, I masked on the Mardi Gras. My sister was working at a factory and they asked me to mask with them and I masked with them and I took my clarinet and blowed that clarinet all day. In the street? Yeah, in the street and they was dancing behind me with tambourines. Yeah. And I was the only one playing anything.
The only one, no guitar or anything.
That was, and at that time, what's that, somebody's getting?
